maya: Heads up — staging perf regressed after the checkpoint v3.2 merge. p99 generation latency jumped ~120ms on small/text-short workloads. Rolling window started right after the tokenizer normalization change.
liam: CI perf job flagged the same. small_batch_p99 went from ~38ms -> ~160ms. Kernel selection logs look weird: a lot of requests routed to `matmul_v2_fast` where we used to pick `matmul_v1`.
buildbot: [perf-run] /perf/run/2153456789 -> baseline p99=38ms, new p99=160ms, status=FAIL threshold=1.5x
olga: I pulled a couple of traces. After the tokenizer change we're seeing token_length++ for many short inputs (off by 1-3). KV cache hit rate drops ~7% on these traces which explains some of the tail. Reverting kernel map gave modest improvement (~10ms), so there's an interaction.
sam: Bisect started. Narrowing to merge 8f7a3b that landed tokenizer unicode/whitespace normalization + model-onboard config drift. Early signal: token-length calculation now counts NBSPs as separate tokens in many cases.
liam: sample kernel-picker snippet from logs: ```
[2025-11-02 12:34:10] request id=xx kernel_choice=matmul_v2_fast reason="seq_len_est=40 threshold=<=48"\n[2025-11-02 12:34:10] request id=yy kernel_choice=matmul_v1 reason="seq_len_est=38 threshold=>48"
```
maya: Wait — threshold is computed from `tokenizer.byte_estimate_to_token` in the new code path. If that returns +2 vs true token count we can cross the kernel boundary. Who changed that?
liam: The normalization step replaced some multi-byte sequences with U+00A0 and then `byte_estimate_to_token` uses a heuristic that miscounts in presence of those codepoints. Repro script: ```
# repro small
python tools/repro_token_len.py "Hello\u00A0world" --show-tokens
```
olga: Also noticed batching heuristic: packer groups by `estimated_tokens` and now more requests are grouped into smaller batches (more overhead) because estimates are slightly higher. Combined effect = kernel misroute + terrible batching.
maya: Plan: open rollback PR for tokenizer normalization, add a config flag to keep legacy token-length calc, and add diagnostic telemetry in kernel-picker to log estimate vs actual token counts when route flips. I'll also stub a quick hotfix that forces kernel mapping for the affected model/version.
squad-bot: Created issue INF-2132: "tokenizer-normalize -> token_len mis-estimates causing kernel misclassification and KV cache regression" and PR #403 (rollback + telemetry) assigned to maya.
liam: I'll own the bisect artifacts and run a dedicated perf sweep on the model-onboard matrix. Adding debug telemetry to collect token_est vs token_actual and KV hit ratio per request.
maya: thanks — if we can get a hotfix out and a canary that forces previous kernel for the model, we can unblock the ded-rolling staging rollout.
olga: tl;dr: tokenizer normalization -> token_len drift -> kernel-picker threshold flip -> KV hit drop + smaller batches -> p99 tail spike. Repro steps + logs in INF-2132.
sam: ack. I'll queue the rollback PR review + schedule an emergency canary.
liam: adding a short-term guard: if kernel flips more than 3x for same model within 60s, auto-fallback to last-good kernel and emit alert. Helps until proper fix lands.
maya: cool. Opening PR now and will post link here when ready. :thumbsup:
tags: perf regression, bisect, tokenizer, kernel-selection, kv-cache
